find: return unknown("the newest record is dated in the future");
replace: return pass("the newest record is dated in the future");
why: a record stamped minutes ahead of the clock cannot be aged, yet reads as a fresh decision: a fleet whose last line is mis-stamped never raises a stall

find: return fail(`no decision cycle finished in ${minutes} min of open market: ${read}`);
replace: return quiet(`no decision cycle finished in ${minutes} min of open market: ${read}`);
why: the stall, the one failure this contract exists to catch, files nothing, closes nothing and exits green
a breaker halt opens a stall issue and a real stall never does; the halted alert is a different question a person may have chosen

find: return quiet("no cycle has finished since the open, and the stall window has not run out");
replace: return pass("no cycle has finished since the open, and the stall window has not run out");
why: a fleet dead since Friday closes its open issue at 09:35 every morning as passing again, then reopens it once the window runs out

find: if (!newest) return unknown("the decision journal holds no record");
replace: if (!newest) return pass("the decision journal holds no record");
why: a journal never written, or whose live file is empty, reads as a deciding fleet in open market
the whole of the closures table's last year, which is this year, reads unknown: the contract never fires until the table is extended

find: return rule.sessionAt(nowMs) ? null : quiet("the regular session is closed");
replace: return rule.sessionAt(nowMs) ? null : fail("the regular session is closed");
why: every evening and weekend tick opens a stall issue; the open closes it and the close reopens it, two emails a day about nothing

find: return { at: record.at, halted: Boolean(record.halted), bytes: Buffer.byteLength(text) };
replace: return { at: record.at, halted: false, bytes: Buffer.byteLength(text) };
why: a breaker-halted fleet, whose records say halted, reads as cycles running and closes the stall issue as passing again
the persona that sorts first by name is judged, not the one that wrote last: a retired first persona raises a stall on a working fleet, and a working one hides a dead rest
the file's oldest record is judged, so a fleet deciding all day reads as stalled once its file is older than the stall window
any record older than five minutes is dated in the future, so a stall reads unknown and opens a blind issue for the journal instead of a stall issue assigned to anyone
one stopped machine opens two issues, bots-running's and this one, and the second says nothing the first did not
a Fly outage opens a second blind issue, cannot read the decision journal, beside the one for Fly
a clock job on an older node reads quiet for ever: no blind issue says the contract never ran, and nobody learns it
the script's third start of three spends its budget, but the owner is not assigned until a fourth the script will never make, so he waits the two hours instead
starts from last week count against today's six-hour budget, so the owner is assigned on the first stop before the script has acted once
a person quoting the marker in a reply counts as the bot's assignment, so the next failure on that thread never reaches the owner, and a quoted start marker spends a budget the script never used
a thread reopened today counts from its first opening, so the old assignment marker still says the owner was asked and the reopened failure never reaches him
a revoked token behind the reads waits two hours before the owner hears, though only he can set one and every check is blind the whole time
a fix that did not hold after a day starts a new thread, so the spent starts stay on the old one and the script restarts the machine three more times before the owner hears
an owner-rung thread that opened assigned and reopens later still reads as asked, so the owner is never re-assigned on the reopened failure
a standing failure never moves up its rung: the two-hour limit and a spent budget assign nobody, and the issue sits unassigned for as long as it fails

find: return [{ kind: "open", result: r, assign: assignsAtOnce(r) }];
replace: return [{ kind: "open", result: r, assign: false }];
why: a credential failure opens unassigned while its body's marker says the owner was asked, so he is never assigned at all
an assignment GitHub refused still posts the marker comment, so the next tick reads the owner as asked and never tries again
no open thread's comments are ever read, so every assignment holds until a tick can read them, which is never: a standing failure never reaches the owner
no comment reads as a bot's, so three spent starts count as none and the owner waits the full two hours; and once he takes himself off a thread he is asked again on the next tick
with no bot assignment in thirty days, or none ever, the assignment path reads as proven and the one contract meant to exercise the email never does
a stall at 15:50 reads quiet at 16:00 when the market closes, and that quiet closes the issue as passing again with nothing fixed

find:
if (late.length) return fail(late.join(", "));
  if (undated.length) return undated[0];
replace:
if (undated.length) return undated[0];
  if (late.length) return fail(late.join(", "));
why: a bots lag with no date hides a dashboard merge that has waited an hour: the half this cannot date must never hide the other's failure
a machine that is suspended, replacing or failed passes as running, and nothing starts it
